card.title: The loan that starts out mostly interest

panels.text: Take a $200,000 mortgage at 6% over 30 years. The fixed payment comes to about $1,199 a month. These are example numbers, not a quote.
Each payment has two parts: interest on what you still owe, and principal that pays the loan down. The payment stays the same, but the split between the two changes.
In month one, the interest is $1,000 and only about $199 goes to principal.
The balance shrinks slowly at first. After 10 years, a third of the way through, roughly $167,000 is still owed.
The twist: over all 360 payments you would pay about $431,700, of which about $231,700 is interest. Later payments are almost all principal.

probes.question: In the early years of a long fixed-payment mortgage, most of each payment goes to...
True or false: on an amortizing loan, the total amount of each payment stays the same while the split between interest and principal changes.
